question_title: BUGZILLA bug feedback uses AMAZON and its reporting IP address is getting bounced
question_content: It seems it is because BUGZILLA uses the AMAZON'S service, but there is now a RANGE of IP addresses that have been blocked, and BUGZILLA have been caught up in this mess. Please let me know which board I can use to report/ask about this issue, if it is no on here.. Here is the issue research (NOTE: I have emailed the BMO_MODS email several times, but had NO RESPONSE, so want to check if others have this issue):   Based on the error message you're receiving, Microsoft is blocking emails from your IP address because it appears on their block list. This is a Microsoft-specific issue rather than an AWS problem.  When you receive a 550 5.7.1 error with the S3150 code from Microsoft domains (Hotmail, Outlook), it means Microsoft's filtering systems have identified your IP address as a source of problematic traffic. Even though you're using a managed dedicated IP and haven't intentionally violated any policies, there are several reasons this could occur:  The IP address may have a poor reputation due to previous usage by another customer, spam complaints from recipients, high bounce rates, or sending patterns that Microsoft's algorithms flag as suspicious. Sometimes legitimate senders get caught in these filters.  To resolve this issue, you should: Contact Microsoft directly using the troubleshooting link provided in the error message (mail.live.com/mail/troubleshooting.aspx) to request delisting Review your email sending practices to ensure you're following best practices (proper authentication, low complaint rates, engaged recipient lists) Consider contacting AWS Support to discuss your dedicated IP's reputation and whether a new IP might be warranted Ensure your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are properly configured Microsoft maintains their own independent block lists and reputation systems, so even with AWS's managed infrastructure, you may need to work directly with Microsoft to resolve deliverability issues to their domains.

I delete messages and compact folders. on a fairly regular basis to reduce the clutter. There was also a new Inbox sub-folder marked 2026 that I had not created and don"t particularly care about having.  These changes are "un-arranging" my folders and messing with my system.  Anybody have ideas how this happened, and how I can prevent it from happening again? Many thanks. Your help will be appreciated.
